utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Morning all, you alright? Let's get cracking, Monday 25th. Quick stand-up, just run the board and no essays if we can help it.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Morning. Sorry, traffic on the ring road was horrendous, proper standstill by the slip, so if I sound a bit grumpy that's why.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: You and everyone else. There is a birthday cake in the office though, so, you know, morale's recovered a bit.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Yeah and whose new car is that in the car park? The grey one. Looks way too clean for this place.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: Won't be mine, mine still sounds like a bag of bolts.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Right, focus, cake and cars later. Any carry-overs, completions, blockers?

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: From me, I tested the new line yesterday and it's all fine now, so that's done, nothing else needed there.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: I signed off the inspection on the Atlas on Tuesday, so that's closed out as well.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: And I already swapped the filter on the stacker yesterday, before anyone asks, so that's done.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Good. I've just got an observation from the floor: I saw the pressure on the pick and place on two dip for a few minutes, it came back on its own. Just keeping an eye on it, not a job for today unless it repeats.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Blocker from planning side, still waiting on parts for the dryer, nothing we can do until they arrive.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Yeah and on access, can't get to the stacker until production gives us a window. So that's still sat there, not ignored, just no slot.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Also, just so nobody plans around it, the shutdown on the MV01 is cancelled now, production need it running.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Yep, noted, MV01 cancelled. Fine. David, anything else from mechanical?

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Nothing live from me apart from the usual noises and leaks, really. Plant's a bit scruffy after weekend but no fresh drama.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Jamie, stores?

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: Mostly receipts this morning. Bit thin on bearings, but manageable. I can look at paperwork bits if needed.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Actually, on paperwork, we need to update the risk assessment for work on the hot bearing. Jamie, can you take that and get it sorted for next Tuesday? Top priority please.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: Uh, not really the best person for that one, Sarah. I can pull documents but I shouldn't be owning the risk assessment for the hot bearing itself.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Yeah, fair. Olu, can you pick that up instead and update the risk assessment for work on the hot bearing, next Tuesday, top priority please?

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Yeah, alright, I'll do it. I'll update the risk assessment for work on the hot bearing and have that done for next Tuesday. If Jamie sends me the latest revision it'll be quicker.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll send you the current pack straight after this.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Good, that's agreed. Aisha, process side?

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: Morning. Nothing huge. The alarm box purchase order still hasn't shown up in the system, which is getting a bit silly.

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: I was going to chase the purchase order for the alarm box, but I've got the solvent balance and the wash trials stacked up this morning, so I'm not going to get near it.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: I can grab that. I'll chase the purchase order for the alarm box by 11am, no problem.

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: Perfect, cheers.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Nice one. Mide's got that by 11am.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: On planning, before we get buried, the FLTs still need a proper slot with production. Normal priority, nothing dramatic, but it does need booking in.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: I'll schedule downtime for the FLTs with production. Normal priority, I'll get it lined up when they're in this morning.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Thanks Doyler.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: And I'll send the shift handover report round tomorrow. I was going to do it Friday and then, well, Friday happened.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Friday happened to all of us, to be fair.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Right. Fiona, separate one: I need you to investigate the pressure drop on the IM1 hydraulic unit today. That one's safety critical, straight away.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Me, yeah?

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Yeah, you. Investigate the pressure drop on the IM1 hydraulic unit today. That one's safety critical, straight away.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Alright, understood. I'll investigate the pressure drop on the IM1 hydraulic unit today, straight after this.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: If you want a second pair of eyes later, shout.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: Might do, cheers.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Marcus, on the stacker, separate from the access issue, can you go to the hydraulics lot to pick up the replacement parts for the stacker after lunch? Top priority please.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Yeah, I can do that. I'll go to the hydraulics lot to pick up the replacement parts for the stacker after lunch.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Good man.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Just to be clear, that's pick up the parts after lunch. Fitting's still blocked till production gives us a window.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. Collection today, work window later when they let us in.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Sound.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: While we're on it, the door switch on two's still a bit suspect. Not failed-failed, but it's not right.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Is that the one that keeps giving the ghost open?

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Yeah, that one. Fairly important before it turns into a nuisance stop every hour.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: I'll order spare parts for the door switch on two. Fairly important, so I'd rather get ahead of it.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: If you send me the part number I'll make sure stores doesn't bin the request in the usual black hole.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Cheers, Marc's handwriting department will try its best.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Good, that's covered. David, anything supporting on IM1 or hot bearing, other than what we've said?

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Not as an owned job, no. I can back Fiona up on the IM1 hydraulic unit if needed, and Olu on the hot bearing paperwork if he wants a sanity check.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Yeah, maybe later just sanity check the wording, because if I write 'hot' too many times HSE will have a fit.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Write 'thermally enthusiastic bearing', sounds more expensive.

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: Put that in a risk assessment, see what happens.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Please don't. Right, anything else live that actually needs agreeing today?

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: No new actions from stores. I'll just support on docs and receipts.

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: Nothing else from process. Main thing was the alarm box PO and Mide's got that.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: Yep. Just repeating back so I don't forget: I've got update the risk assessment for work on the hot bearing for next Tuesday, top priority please, and I'll chase the purchase order for the alarm box by 11am.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: And I've got schedule downtime for the FLTs with production, normal priority, plus I'll send the shift handover report round tomorrow, and investigate the pressure drop on the IM1 hydraulic unit today, that one's safety critical, straight away.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Spot on.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: And me: I'll go to the hydraulics lot to pick up the replacement parts for the stacker after lunch, top priority please, and I'll order spare parts for the door switch on two, fairly important.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Yep, that's the lot.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: No one wants me to do anything, which is suspicious.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Enjoy it while it lasts.

utterances.speaker: Jamie Brennan
utterances.text: He can cut the cake, that's his task.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Finally, a role worthy of my talents.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Right, before we descend completely: watch the pick and place on two, but no action unless it drops again. Dryer remains blocked on parts. MV01 shutdown cancelled. Stacker access still waiting on production window.

utterances.speaker: Fiona Doyle
utterances.text: I'll note those in the planner comments so nobody turns them into phantom jobs.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Perfect. Anything urgent anyone's missed?

utterances.speaker: Aisha Begum
utterances.text: Nope.

utterances.speaker: Olumide Adeyemi
utterances.text: All good.

utterances.speaker: Marcus Hale
utterances.text: Fine by me.

utterances.speaker: David Whitfield
utterances.text: Just the cake, still urgent.

utterances.speaker: Sarah Okafor
utterances.text: Meeting over. Go on then, five minutes for cake and then back out.
